t.1.35.1: When that sage had finished speaking, the two heroes, Rāghava and Lakṣmaṇa, both applauded the tale and spoke to the foremost of sages.
t.1.35.2: O Brahman, this supreme account, full of dharma, has been told by you. Now you should tell me, the eldest, about the daughter of the king of mountains.
t.1.35.4: O knower of dharma, how did Gaṅgā, the best of rivers, become renowned in the three worlds as Tripathagā, and with what deeds is she endowed?
t.1.35.3: You know things in full detail; tell me in detail of her origin among gods and men. For what reason would she, the purifier of the worlds, purify the three paths?
t.1.35.5: When Kākutstha had spoken thus, Viśvāmitra, rich in austerities, related the whole story in full in the midst of the sages.
t.1.35.6: Long ago, O Rāma, the blue-throated Śitikaṇṭha, great in austerity, having married, saw the goddess and, with desire, began to unite with her in love.
t.1.35.7: A hundred divine years passed for the blue-throated god, and yet, O Rāma, scorcher of foes, no son was born of her.
t.1.35.8: Then the gods, led by Pitāmaha, became deeply alarmed and said: "Whatever being is born here, who will be able to withstand it?"
t.1.35.9: All the gods approached, bowed down and said this: “O God of gods, O Mahādeva, you who are devoted to the welfare of this world, moved by the prostration of the gods, please grant us your favour.”
t.1.35.11: For the sake of the welfare of the three worlds, hold your seed within your own energy. Protect all these worlds; you ought not to bring them to destruction.
t.1.35.10: The worlds will not be able to bear your energy, O best of gods. Endowed with the austerity of Brahman, practise austerity together with the Goddess.
t.1.35.12: Having heard the words of the deities, the great lord of all the worlds said to them all, "So be it," and then he spoke these words again.
t.1.35.13: Together with Umā, I shall hold my energy within my own energy itself. O gods, let the earth too attain peace.
t.1.35.15: Thus addressed, the gods then replied to the bull-bannered one: "This energy of yours that has been stirred up, the Earth shall bear it."
t.1.35.14: This unsurpassed energy of mine, which has been stirred from its place, who will bear it? Tell me that, O best of gods.
t.1.35.16: Thus addressed, the lord of the gods released it upon the surface of the earth, and by that energy the earth, together with its mountains and forests, was pervaded.
t.1.35.17: Then the gods spoke these words once more to Hutāśana: "Accompanied by Vāyu, enter this great and fierce energy of Rudra."
t.1.35.18: When that was again pervaded by Agni, a white mountain came into being, and also a divine thicket of reeds resembling fire and the sun, where the greatly radiant Kārttikeya, born of Agni, was born.
t.1.35.19: Then the gods, together with the hosts of sages, their minds greatly delighted, worshipped Umā and Śiva exceedingly.
t.1.35.20: Then, O Rāma, the daughter of the mountain, filled with fury, her eyes reddened with anger, spoke these words to the thirty gods and cursed them all.
t.1.35.21: Since I was stopped even though I had united with my husband out of desire for a son, you shall not beget offspring in your own wives. From this day forward may your wives be childless.
t.1.35.22: Having spoken thus to all the gods, she cursed the Earth as well: “O Earth, you shall not keep a single form, and you shall be the wife of many.”
t.1.35.23: And you, O most foolish one, defiled by my anger, shall never obtain the joy that comes from a son, since you did not desire a son of mine.
t.1.35.24: Then, seeing all those gods abashed, the lord of the gods set out to go toward the quarter guarded by Varuṇa.
t.1.35.25: Having gone there together with the Goddess, Maheśvara engaged in austerities on the northern flank of that mountain, on a peak that rises from Himavat.
t.1.35.26: Thus, Rāma, the detailed account of the mountain's daughter has been told to you. Now, together with Lakṣmaṇa, hear from me how Gaṅgā came forth.
